questions.prompt: Explain why using five well-spaced masses gives a more useful measurement of k than using only two nearby masses. Refer to slope, measurement resolution, and R2.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: The response should connect multiple well-spaced data points to a more stable slope and a visible test of linearity. questions.prompt: Write a claim-evidence-reasoning conclusion evaluating whether Spring A follows Hooke's law. Cite force-extension data, the best-fit slope and R2, and your mystery-mass result. State the range over which your claim is supported.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Grading feedback: The claim applies only to the tested elastic range. BusyBee scoring: Award points only in 0.5-point increments, including whole points, from 0 to the question maximum. Select a rubric-supported allowed score; never report hundredths such as 2.85/3. Do not average or percentage-scale rubric criteria into an off-grid score. A binary completion rubric still permits only 0 or full credit. Allowed scores for this question: 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3.
a. Full credit: Gives a clear claim, cites accurate table and fit evidence, explains proportionality through F = kx, uses the mystery-mass result as a check, and limits the conclusion to the tested range. Partial credit: Gives a supported conclusion but omits one major evidence source or limitation. No credit: Gives an unsupported claim or reverses the force-extension relationship.
